headline: LPA Inside PAR Enhances Habagat as Friday Class Suspensions Expand
seoTitle: LPA Enhances Habagat; August 28 Class Suspensions | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA monitored a low-pressure area east of Northern Luzon as the southwest monsoon brought heavy rain and class suspensions across parts of Luzon.
deck: A developing low-pressure area strengthened the southwest monsoon while local governments suspended in-person classes in rain-affected communities.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA monitored a low-pressure area east of Northern Luzon on August 28 as the southwest monsoon continued to bring heavy rain over western sections of Luzon.
Local governments announced class suspensions or shifts away from face-to-face instruction in rain-affected areas as flood and landslide risks increased.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The weather system later became part of a sequence of disturbances that strengthened the monsoon over the following days. The main public hazard on August 28 was persistent rainfall rather than a direct cyclone landfall.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Repeated monsoon rain had already saturated catchments in Central and Western Luzon, increasing the risk that additional rainfall could cause rapid flooding, road disruption and slope failures.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Residents were advised to follow PAGASA rainfall warnings and their own LGU or school announcements because suspension coverage and warning levels could change during the day.
